# Specifications

Specifications define what the system must do before implementation details
take over. Create one for behavior that changes a public API, crosses module
boundaries, introduces a durable data format, or has meaningful operational
constraints.

Use a short kebab-case filename such as `retry-policy.md`. Each specification
should contain:

1. **Status and owner** — Draft, Accepted, Implemented, or Superseded.
2. **Problem** — the user or system need, without prescribing a solution.
3. **Goals and non-goals** — the exact boundary of the work.
4. **Proposed behavior** — public API, inputs, outputs, errors, and examples.
5. **Invariants and constraints** — properties every implementation must keep.
6. **Acceptance criteria** — externally observable pass/fail conditions.
7. **Open questions** — unresolved decisions that block acceptance.

After the specification is accepted, create a linked implementation plan in
[`../plans/`](../plans/README.md). Keep code snippets small enough to clarify
the contract; production code still belongs under `src/`.

See [`event-pipeline.md`](event-pipeline.md) for the pipeline contract.

name: CI

on:
  push:
  pull_request:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Lint levels live in `[workspace.lints]` in the root Cargo.toml so local and
  # CI runs agree; don't add a blanket RUSTFLAGS here.
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always

jobs:
  rust:
    name: Rust
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # This job executes repository code (cargo build/test); don't persist
          # the token in git config.
          persist-credentials: false
          submodules: recursive

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt, clippy

      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-llvm-cov

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2

      - name: Test published checksum selection
        run: python3 .github/scripts/test_release_checksum.py

      - name: Check formatting
        run: cargo fmt --all -- --check

      - name: Clippy
        run: cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings

      - name: Build
        run: cargo build --all-targets --all-features

      - name: Test
        run: cargo test --all-features

      - name: Test default features
        run: cargo test

      # `cargo build --all-targets` only *compiles* an example. `AGENTS.md`
      # promises `cargo run -p tinyeventqueues --example basic` works, and a compiled
      # example can still fail on its first line.
      - name: Run the bundled example
        run: cargo run -p tinyeventqueues --example basic

      # `crates/tinyeventqueues-bus` exists so a host can name the payload types
      # without compiling the module. That promise is invisible in a diff,
      # because a forbidden dependency arrives transitively through a feature
      # someone enabled one crate away — so it is asserted rather than
      # documented.
      #
      # The FORWARD form is required. `cargo tree -i <crate> -p tinyeventqueues-bus`
      # discards the `-p` scope, prints the whole-workspace inverse tree, and
      # exits 0 looking clean even when this crate is the one at fault.
      - name: Assert the contract crate stays transport-free
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          forbidden="$(cargo tree -p tinyeventqueues-bus -e normal,build --prefix none \
            | grep -Ei 'tinybus|tokio|reqwest|ureq|hyper|rusqlite|git2' || true)"
          if [ -n "$forbidden" ]; then
            echo "tinyeventqueues-bus pulled in a dependency its manifest forbids:" >&2
            echo "$forbidden" >&2
            echo >&2
            echo "The contract is what a host compiles against. It must stay free" >&2
            echo "of transports, async runtimes, HTTP clients and native libraries." >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Require 90% line coverage in every source file
        run: .github/scripts/check-file-coverage.sh 90 coverage.json

      - name: Upload coverage report
        if: ${{ always() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: coverage-json
          path: coverage.json
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  docs:
    name: Docs
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          submodules: recursive

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2

      - name: Build documentation
        env:
          RUSTDOCFLAGS: -D warnings
        run: cargo doc --no-deps --all-features

  msrv:
    name: Minimum supported Rust version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          submodules: recursive

      # `rust-version` is inherited from `[workspace.package]`, so every member
      # reports the same value. Read it off the package the module ships as
      # rather than off `packages[0]`, whose order cargo does not promise.
      - name: Read rust-version from Cargo.toml
        id: msrv
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          msrv="$(cargo metadata --format-version 1 --no-deps \
            | jq -r '.packages[] | select(.name == "tinyeventqueues") | .rust_version')"
          if [[ -z "$msrv" || "$msrv" == "null" ]]; then
            echo "workspace.package.rust-version is not set in Cargo.toml" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "version=$msrv" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.msrv.outputs.version }}

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2

      - name: Build with the declared MSRV
        run: cargo build --all-targets --all-features

  supply-chain:
    name: Supply chain
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          submodules: recursive

      - name: Check advisories, licenses, bans, and sources
        uses: EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action@v2
        with:
          command: check all

# Documentation

This directory holds documentation that does not belong in rustdoc: the shape
of the system, the reasoning behind it, and the constraints a reader needs
before touching the code. API reference lives in doc comments next to the code,
where it cannot drift.

## Layout

```text
docs/
├── README.md      # this index
├── specs/         # behavior and architecture specifications
├── plans/         # implementation plans derived from approved specs
└── adr/           # architecture decision records, numbered and immutable
```

- **[`specs/`](specs/README.md)** — one file per feature, module, or subsystem,
  describing its behavior, public surface, invariants, and acceptance criteria.
- **[`plans/`](plans/README.md)** — implementation-ordered, test-first steps for
  delivering an approved specification. Plans name exact files and verification
  commands, and are updated as the work progresses.
- **`adr/`** — a dated record per significant decision. Use
  [`adr/0001-record-architecture-decisions.md`](adr/0001-record-architecture-decisions.md)
  as the template. An accepted ADR is not edited; it is superseded by a later
  one.

Complex modules also carry a module-level `README.md` inside `src/<module>/`
covering their design, public surface, and important constraints.

The pipeline contract is [`specs/event-pipeline.md`](specs/event-pipeline.md),
delivered in the order of [`plans/event-pipeline.md`](plans/event-pipeline.md).
The module-release contract is in
[`specs/tinybus-module-release.md`](specs/tinybus-module-release.md), with its
implementation sequence in
[`plans/tinybus-module-release.md`](plans/tinybus-module-release.md).

## Conventions

- Keep every Markdown file at 500 lines or fewer. When a topic outgrows that,
  split it into focused files and link them from the nearest `README.md`.
- Update documentation in the same commit as the behavior it describes.
- Prefer a concrete example over an abstract description.
- Link between documents rather than duplicating content; one fact lives in one
  place.
- Write a specification before a plan: the spec defines the outcome and
  constraints, while the plan defines the implementation sequence.

# 1. Record architecture decisions

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-08-10

## Context

Significant technical decisions — the module boundaries, the error strategy,
the choice of a runtime or a dependency — are made once and then relied on for
years. Without a record, the reasoning is lost, and the decision gets
relitigated or silently reversed by whoever touches the code next. Commit
messages are too granular and pull request threads are too easy to lose.

## Decision

Record each significant architectural decision as a numbered file in
`docs/adr/`, using this document's structure: context, decision, consequences.

- Number files sequentially: `0002-...`, `0003-...`.
- An accepted ADR is immutable. To change a decision, write a new ADR and set
  the old one's status to `Superseded by <n>`.
- Statuses are `Proposed`, `Accepted`, `Superseded by <n>`, or `Rejected`.
- Write an ADR when a decision is hard to reverse, constrains future work, or
  will surprise a reader of the code. Routine implementation choices do not
  need one.

## Consequences

- New contributors can read why the system is shaped the way it is, in order.
- Reversing a decision is explicit and reviewable rather than incidental.
- There is a small ongoing cost: one short document per significant decision.

Copy this file as the template for the next ADR, and delete this one only if
the project genuinely does not want decision records.

# Inbound Event Pipeline

**Status:** Implemented, in the order of [the plan](../plans/event-pipeline.md). **Owner:** tinyeventqueues.

## Problem

An agent with access to chat channels (web chat, Telegram, Discord, Slack),
connector triggers (X replies through Composio), webhooks and notifications
receives far more events than it should act on. Handing each one straight to
the agent wastes turns on noise, lets one chatty source starve the rest, loses
events on a crash between the platform acknowledgement and the work, and
replays events a platform redelivers after a restart.

A person filters the same stream without thinking: they answer direct
questions now, skim group chatter, batch the newsletter, ignore the bot that
keeps repeating itself, and read the backlog as a summary.

## Goals and non-goals

Goals:

- durably queue every inbound event before the platform is acknowledged;
- recognize redeliveries across restarts;
- filter deterministically first, and ask a model only for borderline cases,
  within a budget;
- deliver work to the host one turn per conversation at a time, in order,
  with interactive work never stuck behind a background flood;
- bound how much a scheduled source costs per tick, without dropping the rest;
- make every drop, deferral and dead letter observable, with a reason.

Non-goals: talking to platforms (hosts normalize events into the envelope and
acknowledge platforms), running the agent, exactly-once delivery (delivery is
at least once and turns carry stable ids), and choosing a storage backend
(the pipeline runs over the `tinystoragedrivers` ports).

## Pipeline

```text
ingress → normalize → gate → coalesce → salience → attention lanes
        → cadence / ingestion budget → dispatch (host Deliver callback)
```

### 1. Ingress

`Ingest` validates each envelope (non-empty `event_id`, `source`,
`conversation_key`, sender id; keys at most 512 bytes; invalid → `dropped`
with `invalid_envelope`), then enqueues the raw envelope on the ingress queue
with the dedupe key `source:event_id`. It returns only after that durable
write, so the caller acknowledges the platform after it. The response says per
event whether it was `accepted`, a `duplicate`, or `dropped`, and whether the
platform may be acknowledged now (`ack_platform`).

Redeliveries:

- when the queue backend dedupes (`QueueFeatures::dedupe`), the ingress queue's
  manifest `dedupe_window_ms` (30 days shipped) is the completion tombstone:
  the key is rejected while the message is held and for the window after it is
  processed, and the record lives in storage, so it survives a restart;
- when it does not (a broker), the pipeline keeps its own tombstones in the
  document store for `ingress.tombstone_ttl_ms`, written after the enqueue, and
  also rejects events whose terminal outcome is still recorded. A crash between
  the enqueue and the tombstone can let one redelivery through; nothing is ever
  lost.

### 2. Gate (deterministic, no model)

In order, first verdict wins:

1. self-echo (`sender.is_self`) → `dropped` / `self_echo`;
2. sender deny list → `dropped` / `sender_denied`; an allow list that does not
   name the sender → `dropped` / `sender_not_allowed`;
3. direct-message and group policy → `dropped` / `direct_messages_disabled` or
   `groups_disabled`;
4. bot-loop guard: more than `max_events` events within `window_ms` between
   the same bot pair (default 20 per 60 s) → `dropped` / `bot_loop`;
5. token buckets per sender, per conversation and per source, persisted in the
   document store; an event over a bucket is not dropped but spilled to the
   digest lane with `rate_limited`;
6. group chatter not addressed to the agent → `context`: appended to the
   conversation's ambient buffer (bounded), surfaced with its next real turn,
   never silently dropped.

### 3. Coalesce

A durable debounce buffer keyed by `(conversation_key, thread_key, sender)`.
A buffer flushes `debounce_ms` after its last event or `max_wait_ms` after its
first, whichever is earlier. Media and control commands flush immediately.
Events of different threads are never merged; order within a key is preserved.
An `edit` amends the pending event it targets, a `delete` retracts it (both
events end `dropped` / `retracted_by_sender`).

### 4. Salience

Rule features — addressed to the agent, direct message, known contact,
keywords, source weight, recency — give a score from 0 to 100. Habituation: a
near-duplicate of recent content from the same source (`SimHash` over a sliding
window) has its score decayed. Only scores inside the configured borderline
band go to the host's `ClassifySalience` (noise / fyi / actionable / urgent),
within a per-window budget; outside the band or over budget, the rule score
stands.

### 5. Attention lanes

`interactive` (direct messages, mentions, web chat), `actionable`,
`background` and `digest`, each a manifest queue. A turn's queue group is its
conversation, so a conversation has at most one turn in flight; each lane has
a global concurrency limit. Interactive work is dispatched first. A full lane
spills to `digest` (`lane_overflow`), never drops; the digest lane delivers
one turn that folds many events, which the host summarizes.

### 6. Cadence and ingestion budgets

Each source or lane has a cadence: `instant`, `every(<duration>)` or
`cron("<expr>")`. Scheduled cadences accumulate and release one batch per
tick. Each cadence has an ingestion budget (turns per tick, or per second for
`instant`). Over budget, items stay queued with `not_before = next tick`
(`deferred` / `over_budget`): a conversation's pending items fold into one
entry, and backlog beyond the budget folds into the digest. An `instant`
source over budget degrades to a short debounce window and returns to instant
once under budget. The scheduler persists each cadence's next due tick in the
document store, so a restart neither skips nor double-fires a tick. Salience
can promote an item from a scheduled lane to instant.

### 7. Dispatch

The host's `Deliver` callback receives a `Turn`: a stable `turn_id`, the lane,
the conversation and thread, its events oldest first, ambient context, and the
events whose platform acknowledgement waits on it. Per-source ack policy:
`after_ingest` (acknowledged when `Ingest` returns), `after_dispatch` (when
`Deliver` accepts), `after_turn` (when the host's `Deliver` completes the
agent turn). `retry` responses back off through the queue's nack; a turn that
uses up its manifest `max_attempts`, or that the host rejects, is parked in the
dead-letter queue with its reason. `ListDead` lists dead work and `Redrive`
puts it back.

## Configuration

Two editable, strict JSON files at the repository root; unknown fields are
errors that name the field.

- `queues.json`: a `tinystoragedrivers` `QueueManifest` declaring every queue
  (ingress, the four lanes, dead letters) with `max_attempts`,
  `dedupe_window_ms` and `visibility_ms`. The pipeline applies it at
  construction. No queue name or spec is written in Rust.
- `pipeline.json` ([schema](../../schemas/pipeline.schema.json)): the
  pipeline's tunables, referring to manifest queues by name. Every reference
  must be declared, have a `visibility_ms`, and be used by one role only.

`Configure` replaces the running configuration after the same checks.

## Bus surface

Module interface `ai.tinyhumans.tinyeventqueues.EventQueues`: `Ingest`,
`Configure`, `Stats`, `ListDead`, `Redrive`, `Drain`. Host interface
`ai.tinyhumans.tinyeventqueues.Host`: `ClassifySalience`, `Deliver`. Payloads
are in `tinyeventqueues-bus`.

## Loaded module

- Storage: the module connects to the host's `Storage` objects over the
  storage bus and takes the one scope the host bound it to. Its `teq.*`
  collections are declared by `tinyeventqueues-bus::storage::storage_schema()`
  (owner `teq`, module scope), from which the host derives the grant; its
  queues are those `queues.json` declares, served by the host's queue port.
  With no host storage the module runs on memory and logs an error.
- Configuration: an optional private blob carries `queues` (a `queues.json`
  document), `pipeline` (a `pipeline.json` document) and `timer` bounds;
  absent fields run the shipped files. The manifest is applied through the
  queue port at setup.
- Passes: a module-owned timer runs a pass, then sleeps until the next wake
  (ready ingress or lane work, the earliest debounce flush, the earliest staged
  cadence release), clamped to `[min_interval_ms, max_interval_ms]`; `Ingest`
  and a successful `Redrive` wake it at once. `Drain` runs a pass on demand.
  A failed pass is logged and retried; it never stops the timer.
- Callbacks: `ai.tinyhumans.tinyeventqueues.Host` is an optional dependency.
  Without it classification keeps the scored class and deliveries back off.

## Invariants and constraints

- An event is persisted before `Ingest` returns, and before the platform is
  acknowledged.
- Every accepted event ends in exactly one terminal disposition — `delivered`,
  `context`, `digest`, `dead` or `dropped` with a reason. The outcome ledger
  records it with a create-only write, so a replay cannot end it twice; a
  redrive clears it so the event can end again.
- A redelivery is rejected for the tombstone window, across restarts.
- Events of different threads are never merged; events of one key keep their
  order; a conversation has at most one turn in flight.
- Overflow spills to the digest; nothing is dropped oldest-first.
- Time comes from one injectable clock; durable state lives only in the two
  stores, so a new pipeline over the same storage is a restart.

## Acceptance criteria

- A duplicate redelivery after a simulated restart (a new pipeline over the
  same storage) is rejected, with and without native dedupe.
- Gate: self-echo, bot loop, rate limits and unaddressed chatter produce the
  dispositions above.
- Coalesce: no cross-thread merge, per-key order, media and control flush.
- Cadence: an `every(10m)` source receiving 1,000 events produces at most the
  budget of turns per tick and carries the rest folded into the next tick; a
  restart between ticks neither skips nor double-fires; an instant source over
  budget degrades and recovers.
- Dispatch: retries back off; exhausted turns are dead-lettered and redrivable.
- The no-loss property holds over randomized mixed traffic, and a 10,000-event
  flood keeps per-conversation order, never merges threads, and keeps
  interactive latency bounded while background floods.

name: Release

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      bump:
        description: Version bump to release
        type: choice
        required: true
        options:
          - patch
          - minor
          - major
          - current

concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.ref_name }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write

env:
  # The workspace member that ships as the loadable module. Its package name is
  # the artifact name and the library name; `crates/tinyeventqueues-bus` rides along on
  # the same inherited version and is not packaged separately.
  RELEASE_PACKAGE: tinyeventqueues

jobs:
  prepare:
    name: Prepare release
    if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      crate_name: ${{ steps.version.outputs.crate_name }}
      next_version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.next_version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          submodules: recursive

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt, clippy

      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-llvm-cov

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2

      - name: Check formatting
        run: cargo fmt --all -- --check

      - name: Clippy
        run: cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings

      - name: Build
        run: cargo build --all-targets --all-features

      - name: Test
        run: cargo test --all-features

      - name: Require 90% line coverage in every source file
        run: .github/scripts/check-file-coverage.sh 90 target/coverage.json

      - name: Build documentation
        env:
          RUSTDOCFLAGS: -D warnings
        run: cargo doc --no-deps --all-features

      - name: Compute next version
        id: version
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          metadata="$(cargo metadata --format-version 1 --no-deps)"
          crate_name="$(jq -r --arg name "$RELEASE_PACKAGE" \
            '.packages[] | select(.name == $name) | .name' <<< "$metadata")"
          current_version="$(jq -r --arg name "$RELEASE_PACKAGE" \
            '.packages[] | select(.name == $name) | .version' <<< "$metadata")"
          if [[ -z "$crate_name" || "$crate_name" == "null" ]]; then
            echo "Could not resolve the crate name" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          if [[ -z "$current_version" || "$current_version" == "null" ]]; then
            echo "Could not resolve the current crate version" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

          IFS=. read -r major minor patch <<< "$current_version"
          case "${{ inputs.bump }}" in
            current)
              ;;
            major)
              major=$((major + 1))
              minor=0
              patch=0
              ;;
            minor)
              minor=$((minor + 1))
              patch=0
              ;;
            patch)
              patch=$((patch + 1))
              ;;
            *)
              echo "Unsupported bump: ${{ inputs.bump }}" >&2
              exit 1
              ;;
          esac

          next_version="${major}.${minor}.${patch}"
          tag="v${next_version}"
          git fetch --tags origin

          if git rev-parse --verify --quiet "refs/tags/${tag}"; then
            if [[ "${{ inputs.bump }}" != "current" ]]; then
              echo "Tag ${tag} already exists" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            tagged_version="$(
              git show "${tag}:Cargo.toml" \
                | sed -n '/^\[workspace\.package\]/,/^\[/ s/^version = "\([^"]*\)"/\1/p' \
                | head -n 1
            )"
            if [[ "$tagged_version" != "$current_version" ]]; then
              echo "Tag ${tag} does not contain version ${current_version}" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          elif [[ "${{ inputs.bump }}" == "current" ]]; then
            echo "Tag ${tag} does not exist; choose a semantic version bump" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

          {
            echo "crate_name=${crate_name}"
            echo "current_version=${current_version}"
            echo "next_version=${next_version}"
            echo "tag=${tag}"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Update crate version
        if: ${{ inputs.bump != 'current' }}
        env:
          CRATE_NAME: ${{ steps.version.outputs.crate_name }}
          NEXT_VERSION: ${{ steps.version.outputs.next_version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # One version for the whole workspace: every member inherits it with
          # `version.workspace = true`, so this is the only edit needed.
          perl -0pi -e 's/(\[workspace\.package\][\s\S]*?\nversion = ")[^"]+(")/$1$ENV{NEXT_VERSION}$2/' Cargo.toml
          # `--workspace` re-resolves the local packages only, which is what a
          # version bump changes. `-p <name> --precise` cannot express "and the
          # other member moved too".
          cargo update --workspace
          released="$(cargo metadata --format-version 1 --no-deps \
            | jq -r --arg name "$CRATE_NAME" \
              '.packages[] | select(.name == $name) | .version')"
          if [[ "$released" != "$NEXT_VERSION" ]]; then
            echo "version bump did not take: expected ${NEXT_VERSION}, got ${released}" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Commit version bump and tag
        if: ${{ inputs.bump != 'current' }}
        env:
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add Cargo.toml Cargo.lock
          git commit -m "Release ${RELEASE_TAG}"
          git tag -a "${RELEASE_TAG}" -m "Release ${RELEASE_TAG}"
          git push origin "HEAD:${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
          git push origin "${RELEASE_TAG}"

  native-bundles:
    name: Rust module bundle (${{ matrix.id }})
    needs: prepare
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - id: ubuntu-22.04-x86_64
            os: ubuntu-22.04
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
          - id: ubuntu-22.04-arm64
            os: ubuntu-22.04-arm
            target: aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
          - id: ubuntu-24.04-x86_64
            os: ubuntu-24.04
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
          - id: ubuntu-24.04-arm64
            os: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            target: aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
          - id: macos-15-x86_64
            os: macos-15-intel
            target: x86_64-apple-darwin
          - id: macos-15-arm64
            os: macos-15
            target: aarch64-apple-darwin
          - id: macos-26-x86_64
            os: macos-26-intel
            target: x86_64-apple-darwin
          - id: macos-26-arm64
            os: macos-26
            target: aarch64-apple-darwin
          - id: windows-2022-x86_64
            os: windows-2022
            target: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
          - id: windows-2025-x86_64
            os: windows-2025
            target: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
          - id: windows-11-arm64
            os: windows-11-arm
            target: aarch64-pc-windows-msvc
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.tag }}
          persist-credentials: false
          submodules: recursive

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2

      - name: Verify native Rust target
        shell: bash
        env:
          EXPECTED_TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          actual_target="$(rustc -vV | sed -n 's/^host: //p')"
          if [[ "$actual_target" != "$EXPECTED_TARGET" ]]; then
            echo "expected ${EXPECTED_TARGET}, got ${actual_target}" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Build installable module
        run: cargo build --locked --release --lib --package ${{ env.RELEASE_PACKAGE }}

      - name: Verify Unix module through TinyBus loader
        if: ${{ runner.os != 'Windows' }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          CRATE_NAME: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.crate_name }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          library_name="${CRATE_NAME//-/_}"
          case "$RUNNER_OS" in
            Linux) module="target/release/lib${library_name}.so" ;;
            macOS) module="target/release/lib${library_name}.dylib" ;;
            *) echo "unsupported Unix runner: ${RUNNER_OS}" >&2; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          cargo run --locked --package tinyeventqueues --example verify_module -- "$module"

      - name: Verify Windows module through TinyBus loader
        if: ${{ runner.os == 'Windows' }}
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          CRATE_NAME: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.crate_name }}
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
          $libraryName = $env:CRATE_NAME.Replace('-', '_')
          $module = "target/release/$libraryName.dll"
          $verifyRoot = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP 'tinyeventqueues-module-verify'
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $verifyRoot | Out-Null

          $identity = [System.Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()
          $security = [System.Security.AccessControl.DirectorySecurity]::new()
          $security.SetOwner($identity.User)
          $security.SetAccessRuleProtection($true, $false)
          $rights = [System.Security.AccessControl.FileSystemRights]::FullControl
          $inheritance = [System.Security.AccessControl.InheritanceFlags]'ContainerInherit, ObjectInherit'
          $propagation = [System.Security.AccessControl.PropagationFlags]::None
          $access = [System.Security.AccessControl.AccessControlType]::Allow
          foreach ($sidValue in @(
            $identity.User.Value,
            'S-1-5-18',
            'S-1-5-32-544'
          )) {
            $sid = [System.Security.Principal.SecurityIdentifier]::new($sidValue)
            $rule = [System.Security.AccessControl.FileSystemAccessRule]::new(
              $sid,
              $rights,
              $inheritance,
              $propagation,
              $access
            )
            [void]$security.AddAccessRule($rule)
          }
          Set-Acl -LiteralPath $verifyRoot -AclObject $security

          $verifiedModule = Join-Path $verifyRoot "$libraryName.dll"
          Copy-Item -LiteralPath $module -Destination $verifiedModule
          cargo run --locked --package tinyeventqueues --example verify_module -- $verifiedModule

      - name: Assemble Unix module package
        if: ${{ runner.os != 'Windows' }}
        id: unix_package
        shell: bash
        env:
          BUNDLE_ID: ${{ matrix.id }}
          CRATE_NAME: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.crate_name }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.next_version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          library_name="${CRATE_NAME//-/_}"
          case "$RUNNER_OS" in
            Linux) module="target/release/lib${library_name}.so" ;;
            macOS) module="target/release/lib${library_name}.dylib" ;;
            *) echo "unsupported Unix runner: ${RUNNER_OS}" >&2; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [[ ! -f "$module" ]]; then
            echo "module artifact is missing: ${module}" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

          package_name="${CRATE_NAME}-${VERSION}-${BUNDLE_ID}"
          package_root="dist/${package_name}"
          mkdir -p "$package_root"
          install -m 755 "$module" "$package_root/"
          install -m 644 LICENSE MODULE.md "$package_root/"

          module_name="$(basename "$module")"
          module_hash="$(shasum -a 256 "$package_root/$module_name" | awk '{print $1}')"
          printf '"%s" = "%s"\n' "$module_name" "$module_hash" \
            > "$package_root/modules.toml"

          tar -C "$package_root" -czf "dist/${package_name}.tar.gz" .
          echo "archive=dist/${package_name}.tar.gz" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Assemble Windows module package
        if: ${{ runner.os == 'Windows' }}
        id: windows_package
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          BUNDLE_ID: ${{ matrix.id }}
          CRATE_NAME: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.crate_name }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.next_version }}
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

          $libraryName = $env:CRATE_NAME.Replace('-', '_')
          $module = "target/release/$libraryName.dll"
          if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $module -PathType Leaf)) {
            throw "module artifact is missing: $module"
          }

          $packageName = "$env:CRATE_NAME-$env:VERSION-$env:BUNDLE_ID"
          $packageRoot = "dist/$packageName"
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $packageRoot | Out-Null
          Copy-Item -LiteralPath $module, 'LICENSE', 'MODULE.md' -Destination $packageRoot

          $moduleName = Split-Path -Leaf $module
          $hash = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath "$packageRoot/$moduleName" -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLowerInvariant()
          $utf8 = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)
          [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText(
            "$packageRoot/modules.toml",
            ('"{0}" = "{1}"' -f $moduleName, $hash) + [Environment]::NewLine,
            $utf8
          )

          $archive = "dist/$packageName.zip"
          Compress-Archive -Path "$packageRoot/*" -DestinationPath $archive
          "archive=$archive" >> $env:GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Upload Unix package
        if: ${{ runner.os != 'Windows' }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.crate_name }}-${{ matrix.id }}
          path: ${{ steps.unix_package.outputs.archive }}
          if-no-files-found: error

      - name: Upload Windows package
        if: ${{ runner.os == 'Windows' }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.crate_name }}-${{ matrix.id }}
          path: ${{ steps.windows_package.outputs.archive }}
          if-no-files-found: error

      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - name: Verify native Rust target
        env:

        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          actual_target="$(rustc -vV | sed -n 's/^host: //p')"
          if [[ "$actual_target" != "$EXPECTED_TARGET" ]]; then
            echo "expected ${EXPECTED_TARGET}, got ${actual_target}" >&2

          fi

      - name: Build installable module
        run: cargo build --locked --release --lib --package ${{ env.RELEASE_PACKAGE }}

      - name: Verify module through TinyBus loader
        env:
          CRATE_NAME: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.crate_name }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          library_name="${CRATE_NAME//-/_}"
          verify_root="/opt/${CRATE_NAME}-module-verify"
          install -d -m 700 "$verify_root"
          install -m 755 "target/release/lib${library_name}.so" "$verify_root/"
          cargo run --locked --package tinyeventqueues --example verify_module -- \
            "$verify_root/lib${library_name}.so"

      - name: Assemble distribution module package
        id: package
        env:
          BUNDLE_ID: ${{ matrix.id }}
          CRATE_NAME: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.crate_name }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.next_version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          library_name="${CRATE_NAME//-/_}"
          module="target/release/lib${library_name}.so"
          if [[ ! -f "$module" ]]; then
            echo "module artifact is missing: ${module}" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

          package_name="${CRATE_NAME}-${VERSION}-${BUNDLE_ID}"
          package_root="dist/${package_name}"
          mkdir -p "$package_root"
          install -m 755 "$module" "$package_root/"
          install -m 644 LICENSE MODULE.md "$package_root/"

          module_name="$(basename "$module")"
          module_hash="$(sha256sum "$package_root/$module_name" | awk '{print $1}')"
          printf '"%s" = "%s"\n' "$module_name" "$module_hash" \

          tar -C "$package_root" -czf "dist/${package_name}.tar.gz" .
          echo "archive=dist/${package_name}.tar.gz" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Upload distribution package

  github-release:
    name: Create GitHub release
    needs:
      - prepare
      - native-bundles
      - distro-bundles
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.tag }}
          persist-credentials: false
          submodules: recursive

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: '*'
          path: release-assets
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Create release checksum manifest with TinyBus
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          shopt -s nullglob
          assets=(release-assets/*.tar.gz release-assets/*.zip)
          if [[ ${#assets[@]} -ne 16 ]]; then
            echo "expected 16 module archives, found ${#assets[@]}" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

          checksum_args=()
          for asset in "${assets[@]}"; do
            checksum_args+=(--path "$asset")
          done
          cargo run --manifest-path vendor/tinybus/Cargo.toml --locked \
            --package tinybus --all-features --bin tinybus -- \
            modules checksum "${checksum_args[@]}" \
            --output release-assets/checksum.toml

      - name: Create immutable release with module packages
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.tag }}
          REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if gh release view "$RELEASE_TAG" --repo "$REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "Release ${RELEASE_TAG} already exists; immutable assets are unchanged."
          else
            gh release create "$RELEASE_TAG" release-assets/* \
              --repo "$REPOSITORY" \
              --verify-tag \
              --title "$RELEASE_TAG" \
              --generate-notes
          fi

      - name: Download published checksum manifest
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.tag }}
          REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p release-assets/published
          gh release download "$RELEASE_TAG" --repo "$REPOSITORY" --pattern checksum.toml --dir release-assets/published

      - name: Verify the published module through TinyBus
        shell: bash
        env:
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.tag }}
          REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
          CRATE_NAME: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.crate_name }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.next_version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          archive="${CRATE_NAME}-${VERSION}-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64.tar.gz"
          release_url="https://github.com/${REPOSITORY}/releases/tag/${RELEASE_TAG}"
          sha256="$(python3 - "$archive" release-assets/published/checksum.toml <<'PY'
          import re
          import sys
          import tomllib

          archive, checksum_path = sys.argv[1:]
          with open(checksum_path, "rb") as checksum_file:
              manifest = tomllib.load(checksum_file)

          archive_sha256 = manifest.get("sha256", {}).get(archive)
          if not isinstance(archive_sha256, str) or re.fullmatch(
              r"[0-9a-f]{64}", archive_sha256
          ) is None:
              raise SystemExit(f"archive checksum missing or invalid for {archive}")
          print(archive_sha256)
          PY
          )"

          cargo run --manifest-path vendor/tinybus/Cargo.toml --locked \
            --package tinybus --all-features --example github_module_host -- \
            "$release_url" "$archive" "$sha256"
          cargo run --locked --package tinyeventqueues --example verify_github_release -- \
            "$release_url" "$archive" "$sha256"

# TinyBus Module Release

## Purpose

Generated projects must be usable as native TinyBus integrations and
distributable without also shipping the TinyBus host runtime.

## Contract

- The library builds as both an `rlib` and a native `cdylib`.
- The `cdylib` exports TinyBus module ABI v1, an embedded manifest, and the
  initialization entrypoint.
- The module provides `ai.tinyhumans.tinyeventqueues.EventQueues` (`Ingest`,
  `Configure`, `Stats`, `ListDead`, `Redrive`, `Drain`) at
  `/ai/tinyhumans/tinyeventqueues/EventQueues`.
- Each release archive is named
  `tinyeventqueues-<version>-<platform>.<extension>` and contains only this
  module, its SHA-256 `modules.toml`, license, and installation documentation.
- Each GitHub release publishes a separate `checksum.toml` mapping every
  archive filename to its SHA-256 digest for TinyBus's release loader.
- Release builds cover the stable native Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows runners,
  Fedora 43/44 containers, and rolling Arch Linux where official runners or
  images exist for the architecture.
- TinyBus itself remains a pinned SDK submodule and is not shipped as a release
  asset from this repository.

## Verification

CI exercises the bus interface through TinyBus's in-memory transport, enforces
90% line coverage in every source file, and builds the `cdylib`. The release
workflow builds each native module from the tagged source and records its exact
digest in the adjacent allowlist. After publishing, it downloads the Ubuntu
x86_64 archive through TinyBus's GitHub release API and calls `Stats` over an
in-memory bus.

[workspace]
resolver = "3"
# Every crate in this repository lives under `crates/`, one directory per
# package, each directory named for the package it holds. There is no root
# package: the crate a host loads is `crates/tinyeventqueues`, the same as any
# other member. Keeping the root virtual is what makes that uniform.
members = ["crates/*"]
# `vendor/` holds the pinned TinyBus submodule, which is its own workspace with
# its own lockfile. `worktrees/` holds `git worktree` checkouts of this same
# repository; each contains a full copy of this manifest and every crate under
# it, so without this entry cargo walks into them and reports duplicate
# packages.
exclude = ["vendor", "worktrees"]

# Shared package metadata. A member inherits a field with `field.workspace =
# true`, so the version the release workflow bumps is written in exactly one
# place and every crate moves together.
[workspace.package]
version = "0.1.4"
edition = "2024"
rust-version = "1.88"
license = "GPL-3.0-only"
repository = "https://github.com/tinyhumansai/tinyeventqueues"

[workspace.dependencies]
# The wire contract. `crates/tinyeventqueues` depends on it and re-exports it,
# so a host that only makes calls takes this crate alone.
# No `version` requirement on purpose: the workspace version moves on every
# release, and a pinned requirement here would stop resolving the moment it did.
# Nothing in this workspace is published, so the path is the whole address.
tinyeventqueues-bus = { path = "crates/tinyeventqueues-bus" }
# TinyBus defines the message types, interface macro, and frozen module ABI
# used by the generated integration. Socket and CLI features are unnecessary
# here.
tinybus = { version = "=0.3.12", default-features = false, features = [
    "macros",
    "modules",
] }
# The module-side SDK owns the isolated runtime and exports the ABI entrypoints
# required by TinyBus's dynamic loader.
tinybus-module = "=0.3.12"
# Derive macros for the crate-wide error type in
# `crates/tinyeventqueues/src/error/`.
thiserror = "2"
# The bus payload types are serialized into TinyBus frames.
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
# Positional argument arrays and the module configuration blob.
serde_json = "1"
# The storage ports the pipeline runs over: `QueueStore` (with `DocumentQueue`,
# the queue every document driver gets), `QueueManifest`, `DocumentStore`, the
# injectable `Clock`, and `MemoryStorage` for tests.
#
# Pinned to the released tinyhumansai/tinystoragedrivers v1.10.0 queue-grant
# API, which lets the host admit only manifest-declared queue operations.
tinystoragedrivers-core = { git = "https://github.com/tinyhumansai/tinystoragedrivers", rev = "078d2dee0f299d97dbc22fa7210bd64098a4bf59" }
# The module side of the storage bus: `connect_storage` reaches the host's
# `Storage` objects (documents and queues) for the one scope the host bound
# this module to. Same pin as the core crate.
tinystoragedrivers-busproxy = { git = "https://github.com/tinyhumansai/tinystoragedrivers", rev = "078d2dee0f299d97dbc22fa7210bd64098a4bf59" }
# Test-only: derives the exact governed document grant from lease fixtures.
tinystoragedrivers-bus = { git = "https://github.com/tinyhumansai/tinystoragedrivers", rev = "078d2dee0f299d97dbc22fa7210bd64098a4bf59" }
# Test-only: issues real governed storage leases to linked module fixtures.
tinystoragedrivers-tinybus = { git = "https://github.com/tinyhumansai/tinystoragedrivers", rev = "078d2dee0f299d97dbc22fa7210bd64098a4bf59" }
# The module composes the bound transport with the shared storage client; tests
# also serve storage objects over an in-memory broker.
tinystoragedrivers-client = { git = "https://github.com/tinyhumansai/tinystoragedrivers", rev = "078d2dee0f299d97dbc22fa7210bd64098a4bf59" }
# Module diagnostics; the host installs the logger.
log = "0.4"
# The host-callback trait (`Host`) is an async trait object.
async-trait = "0.1"
# Strict config loading: names the JSON path of the field that failed to
# decode, so an error in `pipeline.json` points at the offending field.
serde_path_to_error = "0.1"
# Module integration tests exercise the real asynchronous in-memory TinyBus.
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["macros", "rt-multi-thread", "sync", "time"] }

# Lints apply to every member that opts in with `[lints] workspace = true`, and
# to every target of that member. CI runs clippy with `-D warnings`, so anything
# set to "warn" here fails the build in CI.
[workspace.lints.rust]
unsafe_code = "forbid"
missing_docs = "warn"
missing_debug_implementations = "warn"
unreachable_pub = "warn"
rust_2018_idioms = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }

[workspace.lints.clippy]
all = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
pedantic = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
# Library code must not panic on its own; tests and examples may.
unwrap_used = "warn"
expect_used = "warn"
panic = "warn"
todo = "warn"
unimplemented = "warn"
# Public fallible/panicking APIs must document their failure modes.
missing_errors_doc = "warn"
missing_panics_doc = "warn"
# Documentation hygiene.
doc_markdown = "warn"
# `#[must_use]` on pure public functions.
must_use_candidate = "warn"

[workspace.lints.rustdoc]
broken_intra_doc_links = "warn"
private_intra_doc_links = "warn"

# tinybus is not on crates.io: the crates name it by version range so a host
# that links this module (OpenHuman's `linked` mode) unifies it with its own
# copy, and standalone builds resolve it to the nested checkout. The storage
# bus crates name tinybus by git; that source is redirected to the same copy so
# the graph holds exactly one `tinybus`.
[patch.crates-io]
tinybus = { path = "vendor/tinybus/crates/tinybus" }
tinybus-macros = { path = "vendor/tinybus/crates/tinybus-macros" }
tinybus-module = { path = "vendor/tinybus/crates/tinybus-module" }

[patch."https://github.com/tinyhumansai/tinybus"]
tinybus = { path = "vendor/tinybus/crates/tinybus" }
tinybus-macros = { path = "vendor/tinybus/crates/tinybus-macros" }
tinybus-module = { path = "vendor/tinybus/crates/tinybus-module" }

[patch."https://github.com/tinyhumansai/tinybus?rev=6b3c5b0cc14b1d07b68055b17a937b11de613efd"]
tinybus = { path = "vendor/tinybus/crates/tinybus" }
tinybus-macros = { path = "vendor/tinybus/crates/tinybus-macros" }
tinybus-module = { path = "vendor/tinybus/crates/tinybus-module" }

[profile.release]
# Cross-crate optimization and smaller, faster binaries for release builds.
lto = "thin"
codegen-units = 1
strip = "debuginfo"

[package]
name = "tinyeventqueues-bus"
version.workspace = true
edition.workspace = true
rust-version.workspace = true
license.workspace = true
repository.workspace = true
description = "The TinyBus wire contract for tinyeventqueues: the inbound event envelope, member names, payloads, host callbacks, outcomes and pipeline configuration."
documentation = "https://docs.rs/tinyeventqueues-bus"
readme = "README.md"
keywords = ["tinybus", "events", "queue", "contract"]
categories = ["development-tools"]
publish = false

# Deliberately dependency-light: this is the crate a host links to talk to the
# loadable module, so it must cost that host almost nothing. Nothing here may
# pull in `tinybus`, an async runtime, an HTTP client, or a native library —
# see `src/lib.rs` for why the transport in particular is absent. CI asserts it.
[dependencies]
serde = { workspace = true }
serde_json = { workspace = true }
# Optional (feature `storage`, off by default): storage ports only (no driver,
# no I/O). The `storage` module declares what the module stores as a schema a
# host composes, so the host derives the module's storage grant from the
# contract instead of linking the implementation. The default dependency
# closure of this crate is unchanged without it, which CI asserts.
tinystoragedrivers-core = { workspace = true, optional = true }

[features]
default = []
# `storage::storage_schema()`, the module's storage declaration.
storage = ["dep:tinystoragedrivers-core"]

[lints]
workspace = true

# tinyeventqueues

External event management and queuing. A TinyBus module that receives noisy
inbound events — web chat, Telegram, Discord and Slack messages, X replies via
Composio triggers, webhooks, notifications — queues them durably, and filters
them the way a person filters noise before anything reaches an agent.

```text
ingress → normalize → gate → coalesce → salience → attention lanes
        → cadence / ingestion budget → dispatch (host Deliver callback)
```

Every ingested event ends in exactly one terminal disposition — delivered,
context, digest, dead, or dropped with a reason — so nothing is lost silently.
The pipeline runs over the storage ports of
[tinystoragedrivers](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/tinystoragedrivers)
(`QueueStore` and `DocumentStore`), so it works on memory, SQLite, file,
MongoDB or a broker, and survives restarts: all state lives in storage.

The full contract is [`docs/specs/event-pipeline.md`](docs/specs/event-pipeline.md);
delivery order is in [`docs/plans/event-pipeline.md`](docs/plans/event-pipeline.md).
All seven stages are implemented: ingress with completion tombstones, the
gate, coalescing, salience with habituation and borderline host
classification, attention lanes with digest spill, the cadence scheduler with
ingestion budgets, and dispatch to the host with retries, backoff and dead
letters (`ListDead` / `Redrive`). A property test checks that every ingested
event ends exactly once, and a 10,000-event flood test checks order, thread
separation and interactive latency.

## Configuration

Two editable JSON files at the repository root. Both are strict: an unknown
or misspelt field is an error naming its JSON path.

| File | What it holds | Schema |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`queues.json`](queues.json) | Every queue the pipeline uses (ingress, the four lanes, dead letters) with `max_attempts`, `dedupe_window_ms` and `visibility_ms` — a tinystoragedrivers `QueueManifest`, applied at construction | `schemas/queues.schema.json` in tinystoragedrivers |
| [`pipeline.json`](pipeline.json) | The pipeline's tunables: which queue plays which role, lane concurrency, per-source ack policy, tombstone TTL, batch size, gate (sender lists, DM/group policy, bot-loop guard, rate limits, ambient buffer) coalescing (debounce, max wait, control prefixes), salience (weights, keywords, known contacts, lane thresholds, borderline band, habituation), lane backlog limits, cadences and ingestion budgets per lane or source, and the digest | [`schemas/pipeline.schema.json`](schemas/pipeline.schema.json) |

No queue name or queue spec is written in Rust. To add or tune a queue, edit
`queues.json`; to route a role to it, edit `pipeline.json`.

## Usage

```rust,ignore
use std::sync::Arc;
use tinyeventqueues::{EventKind, InboundEvent, Pipeline, Sender};
use tinystoragedrivers_core::queue::DocumentQueue;

let queues = Arc::new(DocumentQueue::new(storage.documents()));
let pipeline = Pipeline::builder(queues, Arc::clone(storage.documents()))
    .manifest_path("queues.json")
    .config_path("pipeline.json")
    .build()
    .await?;

let event = InboundEvent::new("channel:telegram", "1001", "chat-42",
    Sender::new("user-7"), EventKind::Message, received_at_ms);
let response = pipeline.ingest(vec![event]).await?;
// Acknowledge the platform only now, for results with `ack_platform`.
```

Over the bus, hosts call `ai.tinyhumans.tinyeventqueues.EventQueues`
(`Ingest`, `Configure`, `Stats`, `ListDead`, `Redrive`, `Drain`) and serve
`ai.tinyhumans.tinyeventqueues.Host` (`ClassifySalience`, `Deliver`). The
payload types are in the dependency-light
[`tinyeventqueues-bus`](crates/tinyeventqueues-bus/README.md) crate.

## Layout

```text
queues.json             # the queue manifest (editable)
pipeline.json           # the pipeline configuration (editable)
schemas/                # JSON Schema for pipeline.json
crates/
├── tinyeventqueues-bus/   # the wire contract: envelope, payloads, outcomes, config
└── tinyeventqueues/       # the pipeline, the TinyBus adapter, the cdylib
    └── src/
        ├── config/        # loading and validating the two files
        ├── ingress/       # validate, persist, recognize redeliveries
        ├── gate/          # deterministic checks, token buckets, ambient context
        ├── coalesce/      # the durable debounce buffer
        ├── salience/      # rule scores, SimHash habituation, lane thresholds
        ├── digest/        # the digest accumulator
        ├── cadence/       # cadence specs, the persisted tick schedule, staging
        ├── turn/          # pending turns and the lane writer
        ├── host/          # the `Host` callback trait
        ├── store/         # collections, tombstones, the outcome ledger
        ├── dead/          # parking, listing and redriving dead work
        ├── pipeline/      # `Pipeline`, its builder, the pass and dispatch
        ├── observe/       # outcome sinks
        ├── clock/         # system and manual clocks
        └── tinybus_module/
vendor/tinybus/         # pinned TinyBus SDK submodule
docs/specs, docs/plans  # the contract and the delivery plan
```

Unit tests sit beside their module as `mod_tests.rs` (or `<module>_tests.rs`),
wired with `#[cfg(test)] #[path = "mod_tests.rs"] mod tests;`, because
OpenHuman vendors this repository and its layout check rejects `test.rs` files
and inline test modules.

## Releasing

Run the **Release** workflow with a `patch`, `minor` or `major` bump. It
revalidates, versions and tags the workspace, builds `crates/tinyeventqueues`
as a TinyBus `cdylib` for every supported platform, publishes archives named
`tinyeventqueues-<version>-<platform>.<tar.gz|zip>` with a `checksum.toml`, and
loads the published Ubuntu archive through TinyBus before declaring success.
Do not hand-edit the version in the root `Cargo.toml`.

# tinyeventqueues-bus

Every type that crosses the tinyeventqueues module's `TinyBus` boundary, and
the names of the members that carry them.

The module ships as a loadable `cdylib`; a host can load it but cannot `use`
anything out of it, so the vocabulary is published here as an ordinary
library.

| module    | what it holds                                                           |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `event`   | the `InboundEvent` envelope every source is normalized into              |
| `ops`     | payloads of `Ingest`, `Configure`, `Stats`, `ListDead`, `Redrive`, `Drain` |
| `host`    | payloads of the host callbacks `ClassifySalience` and `Deliver` (`Turn`) |
| `outcome` | `Disposition`, `Reason`, `Outcome`: what happened to an event and why    |
| `config`  | `PipelineConfig`, the strict wire form of `pipeline.json`                |
| `names`   | interface names, object paths, one constant per member                   |
| `version` | `CONTRACT_VERSION` and the bind rule a host applies to it                |

Two dependencies, both pure Rust: `serde` and `serde_json`. CI asserts the
crate never pulls in a transport, an async runtime, an HTTP client or a native
library.

## This crate sits underneath `tinyeventqueues`

`tinyeventqueues` depends on this crate and re-exports all of it, so
`tinyeventqueues::InboundEvent` and `tinyeventqueues_bus::InboundEvent` are the
same type. A module author depends on `tinyeventqueues` and gets behavior and
vocabulary; a host depends on `tinyeventqueues-bus` and gets vocabulary alone.

## Making a call

Arguments travel as a positional JSON array, and member names come from
`names`:

```rust,ignore
use tinyeventqueues_bus::{names, IngestRequest, IngestResponse};

let proxy = connection.proxy(names::INTERFACE, names::OBJECT_PATH, names::INTERFACE)?;
let reply: IngestResponse = proxy
    .call(names::methods::INGEST, (IngestRequest::new(events),))
    .await?;
```

A host serves `names::host::INTERFACE` at `names::host::OBJECT_PATH` with the
`names::host::methods` members to receive turns and classification requests.

## Versioning

`CONTRACT_VERSION` describes this vocabulary, not the package. Bump the major
component when a payload's wire form changes incompatibly or a member is
removed or renamed, the minor component when a member or an optional field is
added. The payload tests pin the serde representation, because it is the wire
form.

# TinyBus Adapter

This module is the boundary between the pipeline and TinyBus module ABI v1.
`EventQueuesService` serves `Pipeline` as the typed members `Ingest`,
`Configure`, `Stats`, `ListDead`, `Redrive` and `Drain`, and `setup` registers
the object and claims the well-known interface name. Neither the name, the
object path, nor the payload types are spelled here: they come from
`tinyeventqueues-bus`, so a rename is a compile error in every consumer instead
of an `UnknownMethod` at runtime.

`exports` runs `tinybus_module::module_export_optional_static!` with a
`setup_factory`: the factory runs once per module instance and every setup of
that instance (the first and each reinitialization) shares the pass timer's
slot, so a reinitialization replaces the timer instead of leaving two running.
Without the `static-link` feature it emits the descriptor, embedded manifest,
and initialization symbols consumed by the dynamic loader; with it,
`linked_module()` for a host that links the module into its own executable.
The manifest method list must stay aligned with the interface macro's dispatch
table and with `tinyeventqueues_bus::names::METHODS`; the unit tests check
both.

- `settings.rs`: the private configuration blob (`queues`, `pipeline`,
  `timer`), strict, with the shipped files and default timer when absent.
- `storage.rs`: the host's storage over the `tinystoragedrivers` storage bus,
  the one scope the host bound the module to: documents for the `teq.*` state
  (declared by `tinyeventqueues_bus::storage::storage_schema()`, from which the
  host derives the grant) and the queue port for the manifest's queues. Only
  when nobody owns the storage name does the module fall back to in-process
  memory, logged as an error; a storage host that is present but unreachable
  fails setup so the host retries the load rather than losing events.
- `host.rs`: `BusHost`, the pipeline's `Host`, calling the host's optional
  `ai.tinyhumans.tinyeventqueues.Host` interface (`ClassifySalience`,
  `Deliver`) at `names::host::OBJECT_PATH`. While no host serves it,
  classification keeps the scored class and deliveries back off and retry.
- `ticker.rs`: the pass timer. After each pass it sleeps until
  `Pipeline::next_wake` (ready work, the earliest debounce flush or cadence
  release), clamped to the configured bounds; `Ingest` and a successful
  `Redrive` wake it early. `Drain` still runs a pass on demand; passes are
  serialized inside `Pipeline::drain`, so the timer and `Drain` never
  dispatch beyond a lane's concurrency together.

"""Regression tests for the checksum selected by the release verifier."""
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import textwrap
import unittest


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
WORKFLOW = ROOT / ".github/workflows/release.yml"
SELECTOR_MARKER = (
    'python3 - "$archive" release-assets/published/checksum.toml <<\'PY\'\n'
)


class ReleaseChecksumTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_selects_archive_digest_not_embedded_library_digest(self):
        workflow = WORKFLOW.read_text()
        ci = (ROOT / ".github/workflows/ci.yml").read_text()
        self.assertEqual(
            ci.count("run: python3 .github/scripts/test_release_checksum.py"), 1
        )
        self.assertIn(
            'gh release download "$RELEASE_TAG" --repo "$REPOSITORY" '
            '--pattern checksum.toml --dir release-assets/published',
            workflow,
        )
        self.assertIn(SELECTOR_MARKER, workflow)
        source_start = workflow.index(SELECTOR_MARKER) + len(SELECTOR_MARKER)
        source_end = workflow.index("\n          PY", source_start)
        selector = textwrap.dedent(workflow[source_start:source_end])

        archive = "tinyeventqueues-0.1.3-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64.tar.gz"
        archive_digest = "4daf1ad06fdeb8fb5410ff48572aead4db4ce5d9446736bb5637e3083d6a3072"
        library_digest = "718a226caac47b8fd3a570138c6e485dd89367e64a393231afa6428796586494"
        (ROOT / "target").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(
            prefix="release-checksum-selection-", dir=ROOT / "target"
        ) as scratch:
            checksum = Path(scratch) / "checksum.toml"
            checksum.write_text(
                f'[sha256]\n"{archive}" = "{archive_digest}"\n\n'
                f'[library_sha256]\n"{archive}" = "{library_digest}"\n'
            )
            result = subprocess.run(
                [sys.executable, "-c", selector, archive, str(checksum)],
                text=True,
                capture_output=True,
                check=False,
            )
            self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
            self.assertEqual(result.stdout, f"{archive_digest}\n")
            self.assertNotEqual(result.stdout.strip(), library_digest)

            checksum.write_text(
                f'[library_sha256]\n"{archive}" = "{library_digest}"\n'
            )
            missing_archive = subprocess.run(
                [sys.executable, "-c", selector, archive, str(checksum)],
                text=True,
                capture_output=True,
                check=False,
            )
            self.assertNotEqual(missing_archive.returncode, 0)
            self.assertEqual(missing_archive.stdout, "")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
